articles.title: Justin Timberlake Rolls Back the Years on Silly, Sexy and Sincere Appearance on 'Tonight Show'
articles.summary: The singer performed a medley of his hits, took part in some dumb sketches and bared his soul about why he agreed to take part in an upcoming Apple TV docuseries.
articles.content:
A game Justin Timberlake gave a welcome reminder of his varied talents on The Tonight Show on Thursday night, variously dressing up as a "sexy" turkey, doing a spirited Scottish accent and of course dancing and singing like only he can.

In what felt like a throwback to the innocence and goofiness of the Obama years, Timberlake was on top form, taking part in sketches, dance bits and sitting down for an interview to promote the 20th anniversary of this classic album FutureSex/LoveSounds and the four-part documentary series Timberlake that begins streaming on Apple TV on Dec. 11. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories TV Justin Timberlake Documentary Trailer: "He's Not Who I Thought He Was" Music Justin Timberlake Teases New Music: "I've Been Chef-ing"

With the Roots backing them up, Fallon opened the show with Timberlake for a song and dance number, with the duo going through The History of Party Songs. In a segment that is catnip for 90s kids, the tracks covered included Soul II Soul's "Back to Life (However Do You Want Me)," Ini Kamoze's "Here Comes the Hotstepper," Mark Morrison's "Return of the Mack," Montell Jordan's "This Is How We Do It," Spice Girls "Wannabe," Bell Biv DeVoe's "Poison," Timberlake's own "Rock Your Body" and more.

In the interview section, Timberlake opened up about the making of FutureSex/LoveSounds , reminding the audience that that his influences on the album included "Bowie, David Byrne, Talking Heads, Freddie Mercury, Queen, Billy Idol, James Brown, Eurythmics and INXS." He said that on the song "SexyBack" he was channeling Bowie doing "Rebel Rebel" and he had to fight the recording company on the production. "They fought me on it. Well, I brought it in and it was like, 'It's too fast.' I was like, 'That's why it's gonna work.' … [And they said], 'You don't sound like you, your signature falsetto.' I was like, 'That's why it's gonna work.'" blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

On the infamous lyrics to "SexyBack", Timberlake added, "That song does not make any sense. I've said this. It makes zero sense. But, it's why it makes sense."

In a particularly poignant part of the interview, Timberlake discussed his love for and influence of the late D'Angelo, describing him as "my guy." "D'Angelo, for me, he changed everything. You know, he was one of those artists… rest in peace. What a brilliant, brilliant, brilliant artist. But I remember when he came out, it just like everything changed. [He] was a once-in-a-generation artist."

On why he decided to take part in the Apple docuseries — which Fallon said tackled Timberlake's career highpoints and personal low points — the Grammy-winner said that initially he "was really reluctant to do it" agreeing with Fallon that he was "sort of famously private." His relationship with director Fisher Stevens softened his stance and that the doc he has "mustered up some courage to talk about some things that I've never talked about before, that, you know, things that even those that are closest to me don't know."

Timberlake said he found the doc experience "cathartic" and he hoped it would help others to share their troubles. "Everybody's going through something. And I think I've gone through a lot in the last five years that I feel like have made me a better human and a better father, a better husband, a better friend."

In the recent past, Timberlake has had a number of public incidents including being arrested for DWI in the Hamptons in June 2024 and revealing in July 2025 that he was diagnosed with Lyme disease . There was also the cheating rumors in 2019, and subsequent public ridicule, after the singer was caught holding hands with co-star Alisha Wainwright during the filming of Palmer. Timberlake had to issue a public apology about the Palmer incident on Instagram, calling it a “strong lapse in judgment.” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

One sketch that's likely to get a lot of play on social media was "Sexy Butterball Hotline," where Fallon (Rocky Drumstick) and Timberlake (Pecker Spatchcock) played two very sexy turkeys — "the dirtiest birds in the coop" no less — manning an after dark Thanksgiving helpline. A sample of some of the lines from Rocky and Pecker in this bit: "Who says the turkey can't be the one who does the stuffing?" "Is it Black Friday? 'Cause my clothes are 100% off." "I can't wait till you lay me down on the table right in front of Grandma." Good clean fun.

It wouldn't be a complete Timberlake Tonight Show appearance without a "Camp Winnipesaukee" sketch. Fallon and Timberlake once more donned the retainers and wigs to relive their awkward teenage years and play the annoying campers trying to sing a popular song much to the annoyance of the camp counselor. On Thursday's episode, the pair decided to take on The Proclaimers' 1988 hit "I'm Gonna Be (500 Miles)" with Timberlake and Fallon's attempt at Scottish brogue worthy of commendation but ultimately short of passable.

Proving he's still one of the greatest singers and dancers around, Timberlake rounded his appearance with two medleys of his greatest hits. In the first clip he performed a medley of "FutureSex / LoveSound," "SexyBack," "Summer Love" and "My Love."

In a second clip he performed "LoveStoned," "Until the End of Time" and "What Goes Around…/ … Comes Around."

articles.title: Recasting the Original Goonies for 2026
articles.summary: What if we sent another group of kids on the adventure of a lifetime? The Goonies provided the perfect group of adorable nerds that Hollywood has ever produced. Each with a big attitude, a crazy scheme, and a little bit of luck to make sure they stayed out of any real danger. Now, four decades […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google What if we sent another group of kids on the adventure of a lifetime? The Goonies provided the perfect group of adorable nerds that Hollywood has ever produced. Each with a big attitude, a crazy scheme, and a little bit of luck to make sure they stayed out of any real danger. Now, four decades later, the idea of recasting the characters sounds like fun. So, who could do them justice? There is a rumored sequel in the works, so you never know what might happen.

Selecting a cast is not quite as simple as finding a kid with the right look. Mikey has to be adorable and learn to be a leader; Brand has to be the oldest brother; Mouth has to be the wisecracking member of the group, and then that lovable Chunk has to get into as much trouble as possible before everyone is sad they lost. Data has to come up with a bizarre invention; then, he has to say why it wasn't his fault it broke, which is always how it goes. We've got five actors who could add their own magic to these parts – and, of course, we can't wait to see the adventure they have together.

Left with the task of keeping everyone safe (and the older brother for Mikey), Brand has to be the strongest and the physically dominant of the group. Josh Brolin (aka Thanos) easily filled the role. But Mason Thames already has some of that screen presence and is certainly quite convincing. Having appeared in The Black Phone , Incoming , Monster Summer , and the live-action adaptation of How to Train Your Dragon , Thames is building quite a resume. The role of Brand would require someone who could be trusted to protect and look out for the others, while also giving them a hard time. Thames could throw on some modern athletic accessories and with the right outfit, he'd be the new version of this bro.

When it comes to lovable nerds, Jake Connelly could do no wrong. With his twist on the beloved character of Derek Turnbow, Connelly actually made the character even more lovable after he was able to reveal a bit more of his lovable personality. Originally an unsympathetic bully, the change made him a little more endearing. Chunk is the clumsy, food-loving, emotional storyteller who frequently exaggerates his experience. He wears his feelings on his face and is often the most emotional of the kids in the series. Still, he is all about comic timing, and Connelly has never been better with an emotional character that still makes you laugh. Prior to his role in Stranger Things , he was also seen in the short film Between the Silence as Jakub. He's still early in his acting career, but being part of the Stranger Things universe has given the actor an opportunity to show off his range. Chunk doesn't have to be the comic relief; he's just the kid who has to be convinced that anyone will listen to his stories. We're pretty sure Connelly could convince you.

Data is a weird, nerdy little kid, but he has to be lovable; otherwise, he would not be part of the Goonies. Alan Kim has that ability to make a weird kid come across as quite natural, rather than like a kid actor emulating the characters that made him a breakout star. He starred in Minari as David Yi, which earned him the Critics' Choice Award for Best Young Actor/Actress and a BAFTA Supporting Actor Award nomination. He's also been in Theater Camp and IF . Data has to be silly with gadgets, but there has to be something sincere to him. Kim could do that and give Data some silly gadgets. His subtle reactions in Minari show that he's capable of conveying the personality needed to play Data in 2026. Keeping it subtle will be important because Data's inventions tend to have minds of their own.

If anyone can bring just the right amount of mischief and humor and personality to a young Mouth, it's Diesel La Torraca. While best known for his role as Austin Miller in Ginny & Georgia , the young actor has also starred in Little Monsters , La Brea , and the 2024 film Unsung Hero . He's demonstrated a mix of comedic and dramatic acting and can bring just the right amount of personality to the part, which is exactly what Mouth needs. The goofy, wisecracking Mouth of the Goonies, always running his mouth and making fun of everyone around him, even when he maybe should keep his mouth shut. With La Torraca, he'd bring the right kind of mischievous energy to the part, and also could serve to make Mouth seem a little more like a real kid than someone just cracking jokes all the time. His experience with family-related stories also would make for an interesting pairing for a new generation of Goonies.

Mikey has to be the kid who believes in his trip before anyone else. He's got to be earnest and know how to sell it. Mason Cufari would be interesting as the Mikey of the pack, as he already has a good feel for the genre of 2026. Born in 2013, Cufari began his professional acting career at just three years old and has since appeared in Goliath , Law & Order: Organized Crime , Harlan Coben's Shelter , and Fallout . He starred as Young Renn in The Good Half alongside Nick Jonas, and he starred as Tommy Fendler in Lost on a Mountain in Maine . Giving him the role of Mikey would certainly leave the other Goonies in his capable hands. He's got the right look to be on the team, and with him leading the way, who knows what kind of adventure they'll have?

The Goonies never say die, and neither should a franchise built on friendship, outrageous adventures, and kids who refuse to take no for an answer. But what do you think of these picks for the next generation of treasure hunters? Let us know in the comments if you agree with our casting or have your own suggestions for who should fill Mikey, Brand, Mouth, Chunk, and Data's shoes!

South African President Cyril Ramaphosa on Friday attended the launch of French media giant Canal+ Group’s Canal+ Academy at MultiChoice City in Johannesburg. The new pan-African initiative will expand training and professional development opportunities for local aspiring professionals in the creative industries.

The momentous event — which saw South Africa 's leader, Canal+ CEO Maxime Saada and other top level executives delivering passionate speeches on the podium — comes after the company's $2 billion takeover last year of South African pay TV company MultiChoice, which has made Canal+ the dominant player in Africa’s fast-growing pay TV market. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Netflix’s Genre-Bending YA Drama ‘The Body’ Is a Queer Y2K Extravaganza: TV Review Anthony Mackie and Jamie Dornan’s Heist Drama '12 12 12' Feels Like a Bad Video Game: TV Review

"Today, we are celebrating a significant moment in the country's broadcasting and creative industries," Ramaphosa said, adding: "I am very envious, because in my private life I've often said that one day I'd like to produce a movie."

He quipped, "What I'm doing currently, it's OK. But now, you are living my dream."

South Africa is becoming the first market to introduce the Canal + Academy model. The program, which incorporates the existing MultiChoice Talent Factory, aims to reach between 800 and 1,000 beneficiaries during its first 12 months.

articles.title: DC Studios' Justice League Mandate From Skydance Is the Same Thing That Killed the DCEU
articles.summary: Image via WB The news regarding DC Studios over the past couple of weeks has been a whirlwind. James Gunn and Peter Safran are officially out after just one year of their reported ten-year plan, and in to replace them is Jeremy Latcham. The Gunn and Safran era wasn't a bust, as the shows and films they put […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The news regarding DC Studios over the past couple of weeks has been a whirlwind. James Gunn and Peter Safran are officially out after just one year of their reported ten-year plan, and in to replace them is Jeremy Latcham. The Gunn and Safran era wasn't a bust, as the shows and films they put out were mostly well received and only Supergirl flopped at the box office. However, the completed acquisition of Warner Bros. by Paramount, which is now collectively known as Skydance, has led to some major changes. One of the things that Skydance wants to do has hurt DC films in the past.

The fact that Skydance wants to make any major changes to what DC Studios has been doing is a bit odd. With Supergirl as the only project that could be considered a failure, things were going well. Reportedly, Skydance isn't going to do a total reboot, but it's clear that things are going to change. Even if that's a decision you agree with, the news that Skydance wants the Justice League to become a thing soon is questionable when you look at the history of DC on the big screen, so it could be a huge mistake.

On paper, the idea of Skydance wanting the Justice League to be a thing on the big screen quickly makes sense. They're the biggest characters in the franchise and audiences love a movie where major superheroes team up. It's part of why 2012's The Avengers was such a huge hit and is the case for every Avengers movie since then. Like Marvel's most famous teams, the Justice League has gone through several iterations over the decades, so the actual group we'd get in this franchise is unclear. The safest bet to appear would be David Corenswet's Superman.

His 2025 film was a box office success (even if Skydance suggested that it had a disappointing intake) and his take on the character was popular. The sequel, Man of Tomorrow , is still going forward and the talk that a new iteration of Wonder Woman will be included likely means she'll be part of this new Justice League. Everyone else is kind of up in the air. Batman is likely due to his popularity, but Robert Pattinson's version of the character is in his own universe and is so good that it'll be hard for anyone new to compete at the same time.

Skydance CEO David Ellison has reportedly told Latcham that they want the heavy hitters on screen soon. The Flash, Green Lantern, and others along those lines are said to be a priority while they move away from Supergirl and Gunn's penchant for shining a light on less famous characters like Peacemaker, the Creature Commandos, and Polka Dot Man. However, rushing to that concept is a plan that has already killed one universe in DC Studios history, so it might not be a good idea to repeat it.

Zack Snyder was at the forefront of the DCEU. Man of Steel was a solid start and it was followed by a box office hit, though a critical disappointment in Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice . Wonder Woman was introduced there and got her own solo film before Justice League hit theaters in 2017. While Justice League had plenty of problems that held it back, there was a lack of excitement surrounding it because of how rushed it was. Only Superman and Wonder Woman had solo projects, while Batman was only part of a sequel.

Justice League also included the Flash, Cyborg, and Aquaman, who had only appeared in short clips to that point. That's not quite enough time to fully invest in these characters before seeing them come together. Part of the reason The Avengers worked so well was that Iron Man, Hulk, Captain America, and Thor had their own films to develop their characters, while Black Widow had a major appearance in one of them. Hawkeye was the only one who didn't get much development. Even Nick Fury and the villain, Loki, were established when that film dropped.

Justice League seemed like the DCEU's rushed attempt to match the success that the MCU had and the problem is that's the opposite of what made Marvel successful. They took the time and care to present their characters as big deals with stories we cared about. Even in later films, heroes like Ant-Man, Black Panther, and Captain Marvel all had their own projects before joining the bigger team. Once Justice League failed miserably, the DCEU was basically dead and never recovered. It's understandable if Skydance thought Gunn focused too much on less famous characters but going too far in the opposite direction feels like they're asking for a repeat of what led to the DCEU's defeat.

Do you want a Justice League film asap from DC Studios or would you prefer they handle things more slowly? Let us know in the comments!

articles.title: 'Dangal' Casting Director Mukesh Chhabra Recalls Auditioning Nearly 14,000 Girls, Shares Self-Tape Tips at IFFI Masterclass
articles.summary: Mukesh Chhabra, the casting director behind "Dangal" and Shah Rukh Khan's upcoming "King," took aspiring actors and filmmakers behind the scenes of the casting process at a masterclass at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa. The session, "The Casting Magic: Auditions Unplugged," turned into an extended conversation, with participants asking about […]
articles.content:
Mukesh Chhabra , the casting director behind " Dangal " and Shah Rukh Khan 's upcoming "King," took aspiring actors and filmmakers behind the scenes of the casting process at a masterclass at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa.

The session, "The Casting Magic: Auditions Unplugged," turned into an extended conversation, with participants asking about everything from self-tapes and social media to age and the demands of the profession. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories 'Heartland' Review: Jessica Chastain Rocks a Stetson and a Swagger for a Soapy Nashville Noir Brandi Carlile's All-Requests Tour Isn't Just a Magnificent Stunt, but an Unusually Moving Transaction Between Performer and Audience: Concert Review

Introducing Chhabra, festival director Ashutosh Gowariker, whose "Lagaan" was nominated for the foreign-language film Oscar, said, "What I like about Mukesh is his eye for character and he will go to any length to find the actors who fit in."

Chhabra, whose casting credits include "Dhurandhar," Aamir Khan's "Dangal," Anurag Kashyap's "Gangs of Wasseypur," Nitesh Tiwari's "Ramayana" and "King," due Dec. 24, described the casting director's role as a bridge between actors and directors. His work begins with understanding a script and the director's vision, then determining whether a character calls for an established face or someone new.

"There is so much talent in our country," he said. "I send my team all over the country to scout for talent. You have to go to the roots. Our country has so many cultural arts and sub-cultures where so much raw talent is displayed." Directors, he added, hire him for "my opinion, my ideas, not for my data."

The scale of the search can be considerable. For "Dangal," he recalled auditioning nearly 14,000 girls over almost two years. For "Gangs of Wasseypur," he cast 384 people. That film, he said, "changed my life." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Chhabra urged actors preparing for an audition to go beyond memorizing lines and analyze a character's background, circumstances, social position and motivations. "Designing the scene in your head is important. We want to understand the actor's intellect. Please do your homework," he said. "If you understand life, you can understand acting."

On self-tapes, his advice was to choose a clean background, ensure good lighting and clear sound, use someone who can deliver cues naturally, and frame the shot close enough to capture the face and eyes. "I want to focus on your face, your performance, not on the painting behind you," he said.

Asked about social media influencers moving into acting, Chhabra drew a distinction between performing in self-created videos and interpreting a character in a scripted story. "If you really want to take your job seriously, you have to learn the craft," he said, recommending theater as a way to build confidence and develop an understanding of performance.

"It's a part of your life, you've got to deal with it. You chose this profession. If you feel rejected and sad all the time, you will miss a lot of opportunities," he said of rejection.

"Acting has nothing to do with age, talent is the only thing," Chhabra said. He advised performers to keep their appearance simple rather than arrive with a preconceived look for a role.

He urged actors to stay curious about the world around them. "Read people. Talk to people. Understand people. That's more important," he said. "It is all a game of patience and positivity. If it is meant for you, it will come to you."

Questions about nepotism and the casting couch brought some humor into the discussion. Chhabra said he had rejected several star kids. "Whether you are a star kid or not a star kid, ultimately you have to act," he said. Asked about the casting couch, he pointed to his seat on stage. "This is the only couch I like. I'm sitting on it."

articles.title: Barun Sobti, Abhishek Banerjee Star as 'Paatal Lok' Creator Sudip Sharma Swaps Violence for Black Comedy in Netflix's IFFI Selection 'Pushpak Vimaan'
articles.summary: After the crime dramas "Paatal Lok" on Prime Video and "Kohrra" on Netflix, creator Sudip Sharma is changing lanes with "Pushpak Vimaan," a black comedy and crime caper starring Jaideep Ahlawat, Abhishek Banerjee and Barun Sobti that is expected on Netflix in early 2027. Two episodes of the series screened at the 57th International Film […]
articles.content:
After the crime dramas "Paatal Lok" on Prime Video and "Kohrra" on Netflix , creator Sudip Sharma is changing lanes with " Pushpak Vimaan ," a black comedy and crime caper starring Jaideep Ahlawat, Abhishek Banerjee and Barun Sobti that is expected on Netflix in early 2027.

Two episodes of the series screened at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa, after which Sharma, Sobti and Banerjee spoke with Variety . Related Stories Brandi Carlile's All-Requests Tour Isn't Just a Magnificent Stunt, but an Unusually Moving Transaction Between Performer and Audience: Concert Review Rose Byrne and Meghann Fahy Form a Twisted, Heartfelt Sisterhood in Peacock's Mystery Thriller 'The Good Daughter': TV Review

"I was just feeling the need to change my lane," Sharma says. The streaming business, he adds, can keep creators returning to successful shows and their sequels. "Honestly, it wasn't the plan to be doing only grand dramas. But that's how life panned out, which is fine. I had real fun doing it. But it felt like I needed to change," he says. After co-directing the second season of "Kohrra," he says, "I wanted to just give myself more and newer challenges." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"I'm a huge fan of the Coen brothers. Black comedy is my favorite comedy genre," says Sharma, who has long been drawn to crime capers. What he wanted to leave behind was the violence. "It was a very deliberate choice. Because I've dealt with a lot of violence," he says. Rather than build the series around a conventional whodunit, he wanted to introduce the characters and their motivations early and let the audience follow the consequences of their choices.

Since he was taking on a genre for the first time, Sharma says, he knew he wanted to be surrounded by friends and brothers. "I wanted people who would have my back, and I would have their backs, and just that feeling of trust," he says. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Ahlawat starred in "Paatal Lok," as did Banerjee, who played the hammer-wielding killer Hathoda Tyagi and is now Bhaskar, a startup entrepreneur. Sobti, who worked with Sharma on "Kohrra," plays Bhupi. "I knew I was writing the part for Jaideep, I knew I was writing the part for Barun," Sharma says.

When Sobti asked how to approach Bhupi, "'Just be yourself,' he told me," Sobti says. Sharma describes Sobti as "this really awkward, sweet, kind of confused guy," not unlike Bhupi. "The quality of writing that he pulls off is remarkable and he's terrific with his casting," Sobti says of Sharma. "I really hope this show does well for him."

"Finally, someone thinks I'm not just a small-town boy who can play quirky or funny parts, or someone who can only play dark, psychotic characters. I was tired of that," Banerjee says of the role. Sharma wanted him to play the entrepreneur straight rather than join the comic antics, and Banerjee says situational comedy is his favorite because it is about reacting to the other actors, not playing for laughs.

Sharma describes the Pushpak Vimaan, the flying chariot of the Hindu epic the "Ramayana," as "that mythical vehicle that can take us from the mess that we are into a place that we want to be in." His characters, he says, are "all wanting to get away from the morass that they think their life is in, and going for this pot of gold."

articles.title: The Best Gifts for Gamers in 2026: Consoles, Headsets and the Year's Buzziest Releases
articles.summary: Everyone has a gamer in their life, and the holidays are the perfect time to get them something special, whether it’s a new console, a buzzy title, a pair of headphones or an accessory that lets them play on the go. Variety has curated this list of the best video game gifts in 2026, so […]
articles.content:
Everyone has a gamer in their life, and the holidays are the perfect time to get them something special, whether it’s a new console, a buzzy title, a pair of headphones or an accessory that lets them play on the go.

Variety has curated this list of the best video game gifts in 2026, so you can surprise your gamer loved ones with the perfect presents this holiday season.

Shop our list below: Related Stories 'White Tiger Column' Review: Young Resistance Fighters in Myanmar Are Trained for War, but Not Yet for Life, in a Delicate Doc Study 'The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives' Spinoff 'Orange County' Reheats Influencer Beef With Better Scenery: TV Review

Nintendo’s latest upgrade to its flagship console is a crowd-pleaser for all ages. Its modular design means you can play on the TV or in handheld mode, with a bigger, sharper screen than the original Switch. The Switch 2 is perfect for the person in your life who is obsessed with “Super Mario,” “Pokémon” and “The Legend of Zelda.” Some highly anticipated new games are only available on the newest console, while most older Switch games still work on it too.

For the gamer who wants Xbox’s huge library without the higher price tag of the Series X, the Xbox Series S is a great option. It’s all-digital and compact enough to fit onto a crowded media shelf. Still, it runs the year’s biggest games, including “Grand Theft Auto VI” and “Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4.” Pair it with a Game Pass subscription and get access to hundreds of titles.

The PlayStation 5 is best for big, blockbuster games, and it’s the console to beat for anyone who loves an interactive cinematic adventure. “Grand Theft Auto VI” landed on the PS5 to near-perfect reviews, and it’s the only console where you can play “Marvel’s Wolverine.” The experience is top-notch down to the controllers, and the deep library spans everything from family-friendly hits to grown-up thrillers.

Experience one of the greatest video games ever made, built anew for the Switch 2. Hyrule has never looked this lush, and modern controls and smart updates smooth out the original Nintendo 64 game’s frustrations while keeping every dungeon, side quest and secret intact. You can even play Link’s songs by humming into the console’s microphone. This is the perfect gift for nostalgic “Zelda” fans and newcomers preparing for Nintendo’s upcoming live-action movie.

Take part in the cultural phenomenon. Thirteen years after “GTA V,” the most anticipated game of all time is finally here, and critics have deemed it worth the wait. “Grand Theft Auto VI” heads back to Vice City in Rockstar’s sprawling, sun-baked take on Florida. The story follows criminal duo Lucia and Jason, a modern-day Bonnie and Clyde, in a world so detailed it could take you a lifetime to run out of fun discoveries. For the adult gamer on your list — this is definitely no “Mario Party” — no other game comes close this year.

In a return to form, “Call of Duty” has produced the series’ best campaign in years with “Modern Warfare 4.” The new game features a globe-spanning story built around a North Korean invasion of South Korea. The multiplayer game mode lets you play online with friends, and it brings back DMZ, in which squads battle enemies and rival players to escape with their loot. For the first-person shooter fan in your life, this is a sure bet.

Every kid with a Wii’s dream vacation spot was Wuhu Island, the tropical resort where you can skydive above the clouds, duel above the ocean and play ping-pong by the beach. “Nintendo Switch Sports Resort” brings back the sunny getaway spot, updating Wuhu Island for the Switch. The game features 12 sports, including golf, bowling, archery and a surprisingly intense thumb-wrestling event, all played with simple motion controls the whole family can learn. This is the ultimate, easy holiday party game for grandparents, kids and everyone in between.

Video games exist in everyone’s pocket. And with the 8BitDo FlipPad mobile gaming controller, you can turn your smartphone into a handheld console. The tiny controller has a built-in USB-C connection, which allows you to plug and play any number of mobile games immediately. This is the perfect affordable gift for a gamer who likes to play on the go.

What’s old is new again. Vinyl, VHS and now the Evercade Nexus, a retro gaming system built around curated cartridges of classic games, with no downloads, subscriptions or online accounts required. This bundle includes a cartridge with “Banjo-Kazooie” and “Banjo-Tooie,” two of the most beloved 3D platformers from the 1990s. Play the Nexus on the go or on the TV and grow your collection of cartridges from a library of more than 700 classic games, from “Metal Slug” to “Earthworm Jim.” It’s simple enough for kids and pure nostalgia for their parents, which makes it a gift the whole household can share.

Excited about the announcement that Robert Pattinson is the next James Bond? Go deeper into the spy franchise with “007 First Light,” a brand-new origin story from the makers of the “Hitman” games. The game follows a young Bond from his early days in the Navy to his first missions with MI6. It plays like a movie you can control, with sneaky spycraft, car chases and explosive set pieces across luxurious locations. Lana Del Rey even wrote the theme song!

One of the best-selling video game franchises in the world is back with another installment, and “Mario Kart World” is its biggest iteration yet. Instead of separate tracks, the game’s courses are stitched into one giant world you can drive across without stopping, almost like an open-world game. Plus, each race now holds 24 racers, which means twice the red shells and banana peels. The standout game mode is Knockout Tour, a marathon race where players are eliminated at each checkpoint until one champion remains. This game is perfect for the whole family, so fire up the engines and pray you don’t get blue shelled.

A PlayStation 5 exclusive, “Marvel’s Wolverine” hails from Insomniac, the studio behind the hit “Spider-Man” games. “Wolverine” is a full superhero blockbuster, and it’s much darker and bloodier than “Spider-Man.” The game’s story finds Logan clawing his way through the mystery of his own past, and the controller rumbles with every grisly slash. For PS5 owners, this is one of the year’s must-have games.

Imagine “Animal Crossing,” but with Pokémon. In “Pokémon Pokopia,” you can rebuild a ruined world into a paradise for Pokémon — where they can live, farm, craft and just vibe. There are no battles to stress over, just a relaxing routine of gardening, building and making new friends. This game is certainly not for your action junkie friend, but it is the cozy pick of the year, a surprise hit that was well-liked by critics.

For the “Grand Theft Auto” fan who can’t get enough of its soundtrack, this vinyl bundle has 34 original tracks inspired by the game’s neon-soaked Vice City. Artists include Dua Lipa, Lana Del Rey, Travis Scott, SZA, Justice, Tame Impala, Burna Boy, Jennie, Morgan Wallen and Keith Richards. Pressed on two transparent magenta discs with blue splatter, the records look as good on the shelf as they sounds on the turntable.

For gamers who like to talk to their friends while playing — or just like to soak up the sound with a good pair of headphones — the HyperX Cloud III is the solid, budget-friendly pick. They’re wired, which means no batteries are necessary, and it plugs into every console. And controls sit on the ear cup for easy volume and mic modification.

articles.title: 5 Classic Movies That Would Be Completely Different If Smartphones Existed and Changed the Plot
articles.summary: It's ridiculous to think about how many iconic films would have been totally different if they had cell phones. There are many big Hollywood movie plots that could have been saved by a few text messages, a mobile phone call, or even a Google search. Many of the tensest moments in movies happen because a […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google It's ridiculous to think about how many iconic films would have been totally different if they had cell phones. There are many big Hollywood movie plots that could have been saved by a few text messages, a mobile phone call, or even a Google search. Many of the tensest moments in movies happen because a character is not able to contact someone, find someone, or get information at the moment they need it the most. If you enjoy a movie from its era, that's totally fine. Yet sometimes, you can't help but be frustrated as you think about how some things would have gone down so differently if the main character just had a cell phone—and cell service.

But what if we went back in time and had the smartphones of today in some of our most popular movies? Would those characters find themselves in those ridiculous situations? Nope! From Back to the Future to Home Alone and Jurassic Park , check out five of our favorite films and see how they would have played out with today's technology. Some, we're sure, would be hilarious; others might have completely changed the plot!

In the case of this film, a smartphone would have been extremely helpful for Marty McFly. In the second film of the series, Marty is whisked away by Doc Brown to 2015, where things escalate, and quickly so, after Marty finds a sports almanac that could alter things if it were to fall into the wrong hands. However, imagine the trouble that could have been avoided if only Marty had a smartphone. Ah, if only we could watch this sci-fi movie for the very first time again.

First of all, he could research the future, verify the timeline, and maybe even figure out what Biff is up to in 1985. He could even show Doc some pics or videos from the present, although I'm guessing Doc has seen quite enough to be willing to believe anything now. And it would be pretty funny to watch Doc Brown discover a smartphone. He'd probably spend the whole movie trying to figure out how to use it to time travel. Although, then again, if he's going to be jumping around between timelines and altering history, having a smartphone probably wouldn't help much. It might even lead to more potential for Marty to fumble his way into trouble. You know, with a quick web search or a few text messages, he'd be on his way to avoiding some pretty uncomfortable situations.

In Home Alone , the young Kevin McCallister gets left by himself when his family goes on a holiday to Paris for Christmas. Now, back in the '80s and '90s, if this were to happen, it would definitely be a big deal. The only way to communicate would be through a landline, and that would mean being tied down to a single location with that kind of phone. But a cell phone would've made things a lot easier for the family.

Starting small, Kate could have just called Kevin as soon as she realised what had happened. Location-sharing apps could have helped confirm exactly where he was. And what about Harry and Marv? Kevin could have shared footage of their suspicious antics with the police and possibly turned this whole burglary into a viral video. Imagine the bandits becoming viral social media sensations for getting their butts kicked by an eight-year-old kid. That said, the power outage to start with would still cause trouble, especially if Kevin was out of juice. But I suspect his parents would have had many more options in terms of keeping tabs on him, or maybe not losing him in the first place.

Here's where it gets even more fun. Scream might be the best-known horror movie to date about the power of technology, especially a simple telephone. Wes Craven's 1996 film gave us our first look at Ghostface, the creepy masked killer who gets off on inflicting mental trauma on his victims. Casey Becker's opening sequence still gives chills thanks to those eerie phone calls that morph into a horrific ordeal. But just consider what would have happened if she'd had a smartphone.

Casey could start by blocking the calls to slow him down, call the authorities, record any stranger following her, or share her location with someone who could help her. Sidney Prescott would also have a lot more options for getting in touch with her friends and would be saved from being thrown under the bus as often. However, I wouldn't necessarily argue that smartphones would make Ghostface any less terrifying. An intelligent attacker might even be able to take advantage of private phone numbers, fake user profiles, and social media to turn their victims into pawns. As a matter of fact, Ghostface could've used smartphones to his advantage and terrorised his victims in a mobile fashion. Yikes—maybe the victims were better off without smartphones, after all?!

Ghostbusters is basically calling out for an upgrade made specifically for mobile devices. The first film sees three friends starting their ghost-hunting careers after being dismissed from their university positions as paranormal researchers. They go on to craft their own deadly gadgets to capture spirits, but just think how much easier their lives could be with a smartphone. I think the franchise never realised the potential with mobile devices. Sure, we have the modern-day reboots, but even those films are lacking in imagination. Surely, in the '80s, Egon would've had a field day with smartphones and customised them to be portable ghost-busting gadgets. And let's also pretend for a minute that internet and cellular data existed.

And basically, Peter, Ray, and Egon could use their phones to video paranormal activity, look up strange sightings, and contact potential customers. Just picture someone filming Slimer flying around the Sedgewick Hotel and instantly uploading it to the internet. The Ghostbusters would likely be huge stars in a matter of hours. They could even use video calling to investigate the reports before sending out the Ectomobile. And can you even imagine what would happen when the Stay Puft Marshmallow Man stomps through Manhattan? Every single person would be on their mobile phone filming him, and there would be about a thousand videos online before the Ghostbusters even had a chance to explain.

Honestly, I think smartphones could have saved some of the most iconic moments of Jurassic Park . A flick by director Steven Spielberg, the film centres around the idea of creating a dinosaur sanctuary where the dinos are resurrected, only for everything to turn to complete chaos. When Dennis Nedry sabotages the park's system, the electric fences go down, dinosaurs roam freely, and the visitors become dino snacks. But what if everyone had a smartphone?

First of all, Dr. Grant, Ellie, and the others could potentially get in touch with the control room, tell them where they are, and film whatever is happening around them. If someone managed to get the first-ever video of a T-Rex eating a car on their smartphone, it would no doubt have more hits than any human video ever. And more significantly, they might even be able to record Nedry acting dodgily before his scheming corrupts the whole system. But smartphones wouldn't be able to bring the power back online or fix the dodgy security system in the park. And that's the problem. Even with all the technology in the world, there's very little you can do when a huge dinosaur is outside your window. Smartphones would also have made it easier for everyone to coordinate and potentially contain the situation before it spiralled out of control. Additionally, smartphones could've been made with specialised Jurassic Park apps to help safeguard employees and civilians in case there were ever any emergencies.

Turns out, the biggest threat to Hollywood's greatest movie plots might not be aliens, dinosaurs, or masked killers, but a fully charged smartphone! What other classic movies do you think would have fallen apart in the age of smartphones? Let us know your picks in the comments below!

articles.title: Marvel’s First Movie Ever Remains Its Strangest, But 40 Years Later It Deserves an MCU Reboot
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Marvel Entertainment For nearly two decades, the MCU has been the dominant arm of the Marvel brand. And of course it is. After all, Avengers: Doomsday will be the 39th film in the franchise, and that’s not even counting all the TV series Marvel has released, especially since the launch of Disney+. Characters like Iron Man, Captain […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google For nearly two decades, the MCU has been the dominant arm of the Marvel brand. And of course it is. After all, Avengers: Doomsday will be the 39th film in the franchise, and that’s not even counting all the TV series Marvel has released, especially since the launch of Disney+. Characters like Iron Man, Captain America, and the Avengers have reinvigorated the Marvel name in a way few could have predicted in the early 2000s. Despite the ebbs and flows of the Multiverse Saga , the MCU remains in a strong position even now, thanks in large part to the record-breaking success of Spider-Man: Brand New Day .

So naturally, to younger audiences, the idea of a Marvel movie is defined by the MCU. But Marvel has a much longer history on the big screen than some fans may realize. Millennials first flocked to the cinema to see heroes like Spider-Man and the X-Men make their cinematic debuts in the early 2000s, which brought iconic performances from stars like Tobey Maguire and Hugh Jackman. However, for elder millennials and Generation X, these weren’t the first run of Marvel movies. Before Blade and even Dolph Lundgren’s The Punisher , Marvel made its debut movie with the most unexpected character.

Produced by George Lucas, Howard the Duck debuted in theaters on August 1, 1986. The story follows the title character, an anthropomorphic duck and resident of the distant planet Duckworld (yes, really), as he crash-lands on Earth. Howard befriends singer Beverly Switzler (Lea Thompson, in one of her first post- Back to the Future roles), becomes the manager of her band, and, in his effort to go home, accidentally unleashes an evil entity. The movie winds up being a bizarre mishmash of kid-friendly puns, very adult-oriented humor, body horror, and an inter-species romance. Howard the Duck was critically reviled and a box office bomb upon release. Here's the trailer:

In recent years, Howard the Duck has developed a cult following precisely because of how weird it is. The film far predates any attempt by Marvel to appeal to mass audiences, and some fans find a certain charm in the movie’s admittedly dated visual effects and go-for-broke sensibility. Rather than a movie trying to become a mainstream success, Howard the Duck — whether intentionally or not — confidently owns its strangeness. Regardless of how well it succeeds, the movie deserves credit for taking such a wild swing. And as an artifact of a different era of Marvel movie, it has earned its place as a cinematic curio.

Of course, fans might remember that Howard the Duck actually has already appeared a few times in the MCU. Voiced by Seth Green , the computer-generated character debuted in modern Marvel in 2014’s Guardians of the Galaxy , memorably enjoying a drink on Knowhere after escaping the containment of The Collector. He later reappears not only in that film’s two sequels but also participates in the Battle of Earth in Avengers: Endgame . Look closely, and you can see a gun-toting Howard amidst the many Avengers that Captain America unforgettably calls to “assemble.” Beyond the films, Green reprised the role for the Ultimate Spider-Man , Guardians of the Galaxy , and What If…? animated series.

With the future of the MCU still in flux, perhaps the time is right for Howard the Duck to get a second chance at his own feature or, at the very least, a Marvel Special Presentation. Guardians of the Galaxy director James Gunn will soon be departing DC Studios, and since he spearheaded Howard the Duck’s entrance into the MCU, he would be the perfect one to finally give him a second chance at the spotlight. After all, if Gunn could turn a sentient tree into a beloved fan favorite, then the wild storytelling of Howard the Duck — maybe even opposite his comic book partner, Man-Thing, who appears in Werewolf By Night — is right in his wheelhouse. After 40 years, Marvel fans are due another dose of duck.

Should Howard the Duck get more screen time in the MCU going forward? Let us know in the comments section below!

Avengers: Doomsday arrives in theaters on December 18, 2026.

Northern Ireland Screen has appointed its new Chief Executive. Laura Livingstone will take on the role in January.

Livingstone will take over from current CEO Richard Williams, who announced in June that he would step down from the role in December after over 23 years in the position.

The exec has two decades of experience across film, TV, VFX and creative technology. Formerly a Netflix VFX executive, she is currently a VFX producer on an Amazon MGM Studios series. The Armagh native previously co-founded Ntropic London and advised on the business case for Studio Ulster. Speaking about her new role at Northern Ireland's lead screen agency, Livingstone said: “I am delighted and honoured to have been appointed CEO of Northern Ireland Screen. Northern Ireland has an extraordinary wealth of creative talent and has established an international reputation for excellence across the screen industries. articles.title: RECLab 2026: New Films From ‘Alcarràs,’ ‘Romería’ Producers Bound for a Key New Spanish Talent Forum
articles.summary: Lluis Segura’s AI title “Electrónica,” as well as “Mother of Sugar” and “La Unión,” from the producers of “Alcarràs” and “Romería” respectively, bid fair to be potential standouts at the 12th edition of Primer Test, the industry centerpiece of RECLab, one of Spain’s most important new directorial talent labs. Part of the RECTarragona Film Festival, […]
articles.content:
Lluis Segura’s AI title “Electrónica,” as well as “Mother of Sugar” and “La Unión,” from the producers of “Alcarràs” and “Romería” respectively, bid fair to be potential standouts at the 12th edition of Primer Test, the industry centerpiece of RECLab , one of Spain’s most important new directorial talent labs.

Part of the RECTarragona Film Festival, which takes place Dec. 2-8, REC Lab, directed by Javier García Puerto , unspools over Dec. 3-6 in Tarragona. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Fox Closes $22 Billion Roku Takeover, Says Streaming Platform Will Remain 'Open Ecosystem' Fox Commits to Carrying Non-Fox Content on Roku for at Least 3 Years as DOJ Closes Antitrust Investigation

A 75-minute drive south of Barcelona, it sources projects from Catalonia and its vibrant arthouse scene. Producers of Primer Test titles take in some of the foremost Catalan industry figures including Tono Folguera (“Alcarràs”), Àngels Masclans (“Romería”), Ariadna Dot (a producer on TIFF Fipresci Award winner “Forastera” and Platform laureate “They Will Be Dust”) and Mireia Graells Vivancos (behind SXSW hit “Fury”).

At least five of the seven titles, to be screened in post-production as works in progress, are feature debuts for their directors, however.

They will hope for as much success as titles sneak-peaked at RECLab in the past as a important testing ground such as Cannes’ 2023 Directors’ Fortnight Best European Film winner “Creatura” and “Mamífera,” a SXSW Best Performance Special Jury Prize winner for María Rodríguez Soto.

Establiliz Urresola’s “20,000 Species of Bees,” the Berlin Festival 2023 Best Performance winner, was the first victor at RECLab’s Screening Test, before its Berlin selection. How the film should end was decided after that Screening Test. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

“Electrónica,” from Barcelona’s ESCAC film school, J.A. Bayona’s alma mater, marks “an ambitious visual experiment,” says director Lluis Segura, “making AI not just the subject of its story, but an integral part of its cinematic language.”

A RECLab 2026 buzz title, “Mother of Sugar” weighs in as a landmark project for Spanish cinema, led by Andrea Álvarez, an actress with an intellectual disability, producer Adriana Dot told Variety .

The biggest international co-production at RECLab, “La Unión”marks the latest from Àngels Masclans, a producer on Carla Simon’s well received 2024 Cannes Competition contender “Romería.”

“Off Season” reps the feature debut of Marta Font, a director on Netflix hit Spanish series “Intimacy” which was led by “Money Heist” star Itziar Ituño.

Primer Test titles also takes in “Juliette & Camille,” from Paloma Zapata, director of international sales breakout “La Singla.” “Mirage” marks Santa Cecilia and producer Marieta Caballero Baeza’s feature debut; Mauricio S. Burckhardt’s “Another Wreck,” won three of the four post-production awards at Colombia’s Cartagena Film Festival, one an invite to RECLab.

Some titles are well-known. “La Unión,” for instance, was developed at the ECAM Madrid Film School, TorinoFilmLab and Bogotá Audiovisual Market, among other programs. “Electrónica,” by contrast, has flown under the radar. “Juliette & Camille” has been put through nine development programs including Málaga’s MAFF, Guadalajara’s Co-Production Meeting and Sanfic Industria.

Women near double men as the directors or lead producers of Primer Test titles, a sign of the robust driving force behind so much of the now near decade-old Newest Catalan Cinema – think Carla Simón, Meritxell Colell or Pilar Palomero – which grew out of films grounded in a sense of place but addressing universal issues.

Immigration figures prominently at Primer Test. Both “La Unión” and “Another Wreck” focus on the consequences of relocation decades later in the present day, but are inspired by the directors’ real family story of migration. In “Another Wreck,” the director’s own family archive from World War II is woven into the fiction. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

“Off Season” is a “family reconnection drama,” noted producer Mireia Graells. As is “La Unión.” Many of titles capture the contemporary search for identity. Bedrock relationships can be found, however, beyond those of a cisgender couple or biological family.

“Juliette & Camille,” for instance, marks a search for belonging, framed as a relationship to place and intimacy with chosen people in a world in flux. “Without belonging, you’re left with a deep sense of solitude,” says Camille, French but now settled in Galicia.

A closer look at Primer Test titles:

“Another Wreck,” (“Otro Naufragio,” Mauricio S. Burckhardt, Haus Kino, Colombia, Bam Bam Cinema, Portugal)

Silvia receives an old suitcase filled with letters, photographic rolls and clothes, buys a used book and, within its pages, finds a letter in German which mentions a hotel. She goes there and stays a night. “A Nouvelle Vague-inflected romance set in present-day Bogotá,” says Burckhardt from Haus Kino, whose “Meteorite” premiered at Venice Intl. Film Critics’ Week. The feature debut of Burckhardt who directed Colombian TV series “Of Love and Other Misfortunes.”

“Electrónica,” (Lluis Segura, ESCAC, Spain)

One of the most intriguing projects at this year’s RECLab, produced by the evergreen Sergi Casamitjana, head of ESCAC. Max, an electronic music composer, is obsessed with creating music that changes the world. Then a follower, Z3nith, sends him the design of a neural device capable of rewriting the mind. “Blending live-action footage with AI-generated worlds,” but still “a deeply human story about love, obsession and the illusion of control,” Segura told Variety .

“Juliette & Camille,” (Paloma Zapata, La Fabrica Naranja, Spain, Indígena Films, both Spain; Boca del Cielo Producciones, México)

Juliette, born in Barcelona to Peruvian parents and searching for her roots, meets up with electronic music specialist Camille, who crates songs drawn from the sounds of nature. They set out to make together a song over three rainy days at a sound studio in a forest in Galicia. As the song grows, their relationship flowers.“Juliette & Camille” is “a universal story about identity, memory, the transformational power of artistic creation, said producer Sara Horta. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

“Mirage,” (Pablo Santa Cecilia, produced by Marieta Caballero, Spain)

Paris, 2014. Anna and Chiara, a couple, film their daily life. 2017: a homophobic attack leaves Chiara dead. Years later, two friends set out to make a documentary about them from hundreds of home videos; “reality and fiction starts to dissolve into a feverish dreamscape of grief,” says the synopsis. “My intention is to explore that ambiguous space between reality and fiction, giving the audience the freedom to decide what ‘Mirage’ is,” says Santa Cecilia.

“Mother of Sugar,” (“Mare de sucre,” Clàudia Cedó, Lastor Media, Suica Films, Deliris Films, Spain)

María, 35 years old, with 65% intellectual disability, cherishes a lifelong, deeply held desire to become a mother. When challenged, she decides to reclaim control over her body and future and stop asking for permission. Based on Cedó’s Goya-nominated short 2023 “De sucre” and produced by Tono Folguera’s Lastor Media, Ariadna Dot’s Deliris Films and Rafa Moles’ Suica Films, “an intimate, human story with a powerful contemporary question about autonomy, desire and freedom,” says Dot.

“Off Season,” (“Temporada Baixa,” Marta Font, Ringo Media, Spain)

At a beach, a widower and his two children face an autumn of changes, silences and uncertainty, until one night reunites them, ending the off-season. A film about “three people of different ages each facing their own personal crisis,” says Font.

Starring Quim Avila (“Ravalear”) , f rom Mireia Graell Vivancos’ Barcelona-based Ringo Media, behind Berlin-selected “Matria,” and two SXSW premieres: “My Sextortion Diary” and “Fury.”

“La Unión,” (Cordelia Alegre, Dos Soles Media, Wknd, El Sol Ermitaño, Rara Cine, EFD, Spain, Colombia)

After their mother’s death, Cecilia and Juliana, 19-year-old twins, travel for Christmas to Colombia, where they were born but barely remember. Cecilia delves into their father’s past and Juliana struggles to understand her own present. Born by Alegre’s “personal journey to reconstruct her mother’s and aunt’s story, exploring how we build bonds with people we have never met and the silences that shape our identities,” says producer Angels Masclans .

articles.title: 'High Fidelity' Director Stephen Frears Still Teases Jack Black: 'I Told Him, You Owe All This to Me!'
articles.summary: Honored with a lifetime achievement award, director Stephen Frears arrived at the Torino Film Festival in a reflective mood. Over a storied career, the British filmmaker embodied the anti-Thatcher counterculture with features like "My Beautiful Laundrette" and "Sammy and Rosie Get Laid," before earning Oscar glory with dramas such as "Dangerous Liaisons" and "The Queen." […]
articles.content:
Honored with a lifetime achievement award, director Stephen Frears arrived at the Torino Film Festival in a reflective mood.

Over a storied career, the British filmmaker embodied the anti-Thatcher counterculture with features like "My Beautiful Laundrette" and "Sammy and Rosie Get Laid," before earning Oscar glory with dramas such as "Dangerous Liaisons" and "The Queen." But above all, Frears takes pride in his pop-culture footprint, particularly films "that have found audiences and touched people." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Fox Commits to Carrying Non-Fox Content on Roku for at Least 3 Years as DOJ Closes Antitrust Investigation Fox Closes $22 Billion Roku Takeover, Says Streaming Platform Will Remain 'Open Ecosystem'

Chief among them is "High Fidelity," his 2000 romantic comedy starring John Cusack, Lisa Bonet and Catherine Zeta-Jones. A famously unfaithful adaptation, the cult classic moved Nick Hornby's London-set novel to Chicago's Wicker Park and built a soundtrack that film music aficionados still obsess over. Frears is happy to take some credit for the coup.

"I always thought it was a very good book, and that it was really about love," he says, explaining the geographical liberty. Only in crossing the Atlantic, he found a new set of collaborators, steeped in the music that would define the film. "I was very, very lucky. I was already quite old, so I didn't really know the music," he says with a laugh. "Everyone who worked on the film knew about music. So I said, 'I'll sit over here. You bring me the music, and I'll tell you if it goes in the film or not!'"

Discovering Jack Black was another "stroke of luck." At the time, Black was known for bit parts in films like "Mars Attacks!" and "Bob Roberts," as well as his musical comedy duo Tenacious D. His turn as a bombastic music snob in "High Fidelity" catapulted him to leading-man status and cemented a screen persona that has since proved durable and lucrative. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"[In 2003,] he took me to the premiere of 'School of Rock,'" the filmmaker recalls. "As the lights went down, I told him, 'You owe all this to me.' And Jack replied, 'I know!' I recently had lunch with him in London, and teased him, asking, 'Do you have any films that aren't successful?'"

Frears followed "High Fidelity" with 2002's "Dirty Pretty Things," which, in turn, gave Chiwetel Ejiofor his star-making role. The film tackled the exploitation of undocumented migrants, a subject Frears believes cinema had largely overlooked. "It was the first time a film was made about modern Britain," he says. "So many people entering the country were illegal immigrants, and this was the first film to address that."

Having chronicled Britain under Thatcher and Blair, Frears is just as bleak about the country today. "We're broke," he says. "We have no money. You know, it's all a disaster. So the biggest story today is how to sort that out."

He has little doubt where to place the blame.

"The people who did Brexit should be in prison," he says. "These people have destroyed the British economy. Now anybody sensible would like to [get back into Europe], but [the anti-EU people] all still out there making trouble. They're dreadful, dreadful people. My poor country!"

"[Brexit] cost about 5 or 6% of our GDP," he continues. "I mean, it was completely idiotic. You would see these politicians on television talking about sovereignty. Nobody's interested in sovereignty. We have a queen and a king, so we don't have to worry about that. What were all the conversations about? I never understood. It was clearly economic ruin."

Until another project crosses his desk ("All I do is read scripts and pick them out," he says), Frears has been catching up on contemporary releases. Heading home from Turin, he is especially keen to see recent Palme d'Or winner "Fjord."

Indeed, as with Ejiofor and Black, "Fjord" director Cristian Mungiu can thank the Torino honoree for a career milestone. As president of the Cannes jury in 2007, Frears did, after all, award the Romanian filmmaker his first Palme d'Or, for "4 Months, 3 Weeks and 2 Days."

"It was a very tough year, with a lot of good films," Frears recalls. "[‘The Diving Bell and the Butterfly’ director] Julian Schnabel was very cross with me for not giving him the prize. He told me as much!" blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Frears also peeled back the curtain onto that year's jury deliberations, which famously saw the Coen brothers' eventual Oscar winner "No Country for Old Men" leave the Croisette empty-handed. "The jury just refused to talk about it," says Frears, attributing their reticence to "anti-Americanism."

He adds: "But I said, 'This is the film that people all over the world will actually go see!'"

articles.title: 4 Hit TV Shows from the 2010s That Wouldn't Work Today (& 1 Is Still Airing Despite the Backlash)

It was the decade that brought us Game of Thrones, The Walking Dead, and Stranger Things, just to name a few. But going back and watching some of these […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google TV has its ups and downs, and the 2010s gave us several fan-favorite shows that are still remembered by a large part of the audience today. It was the decade that brought us Game of Thrones , The Walking Dead , and Stranger Things , just to name a few. But going back and watching some of these shows can be a rather interesting experience, since not everything has aged as well as we might have hoped. Back then, certain issues either went unnoticed or weren't discussed as much as they are today, but they would be a much bigger problem now.

That doesn't mean these series have stopped being entertaining or that their flaws take away from everything they contributed to TV's history . However, it's interesting to consider how differently they would be received if they premiered today, because their audience numbers and overall reception would almost certainly look different. Curious to see which ones would struggle the most? We've picked 4 for this list.

When American Horror Story first came out, it became a huge hit , and one of the coolest things about the show was how willing it was to push boundaries that other productions, especially in the horror genre, wouldn't even attempt to cross at the time. It's an anthology series that tells a different story each season, with plots involving everything such as a haunted house, a psychiatric hospital, a coven of witches, a supernatural hotel, and more. This format gives the writing plenty of freedom to explore different ideas and keep things fresh for the audience. But on the other hand, that freedom can eventually be a problem if it's not handled properly—and that's exactly what happened.

After tons of episodes of shocking and surprising everyone in all kinds of ways, AHS seems to have reached a point where it just doesn't have much left to offer. The show has always pushed things too far, relying on gore, caricature characters, and real-life issues, for example, but often without giving these stories much depth. At first, this wasn't such a big deal, but as time went on, these problems became more noticeable and started bothering fans . Besides, the show also can't recognize when an idea has already been explored to exhaustion. Even so, it keeps going strong , and the only real difference is that a large part of its audience now spends more time criticizing it, and others have already given up.

Fans of The Vampire Diaries have always been loyal to the show, so much so that you can still find people looking back on it fondly today. It's definitely one of the most iconic vampire productions on TV . Based on L. J. Smith's book series, the story follows Elena (Nina Dobrev), a girl trying to cope with the loss of her parents, who meets Stefan (Paul Wesley) and finds out he's a vampire. Then Damon (Ian Somerhalder), his older and more unpredictable brother, shows up, turning her life into a series of romances, dangerous situations, and supernatural threats involving other kinds of creatures. And well, you can easily see how perfectly this concept fit the 2010s , but it wouldn't make quite the same impression today, would it?

And why is that? Besides the fact that vampire stories (especially those centered around romance) have become oversaturated, the series featured several storylines that portrayed abusive behavior with a kind of charm that people are now much better at recognizing as problematic. Damon, for example, is always manipulating people, disregarding their autonomy, and even using vampire compulsion to control some other characters, which are actions you wouldn't look at the same way today. It's not that characters like him shouldn't exist in TV shows anymore, but back then, audiences were much more willing to overlook that behavior because there was a love story at the center of it all . So, TVD was a product of its time.

These days, Orange Is the New Black doesn't really get talked about , which is pretty wild considering how popular it was throughout the 2010s. One of its strongest aspects was showing that women in prison didn't have to be treated as secondary characters or supporting figures in someone else's story. The plot initially focuses on Piper Chapman (Taylor Schilling), an upper-middle-class woman sentenced to prison for a crime she committed years earlier, as she tries to adjust to life at Litchfield and get along with inmates from very different backgrounds. But as the story progresses, the show shifts its attention to the other women as well, giving us a chance to know their lives and explore important issues such as racism, violence, social inequality, and the flaws of the American prison system.

Basically, Orange Is the New Black was groundbreaking at the time. However, the way it chose to address some of these issues could be a problem today: the suffering of some characters was often a driving force behind the drama, without giving them enough room to develop their own storylines. Poussey's (Samira Wiley) death, for example , was one of the most memorable moments, but it also made people question why the death of a Black character had to be used to create an emotional impact. These are important subjects that need to be discussed, but they also require a lot more care in how they're handled. Some of the show's narrative choices would likely face much more scrutiny if it premiered today.

Today, although they're still hard to come by, there's some variety of musical shows , but back then, Glee was one of the pioneers of the format, which is why it managed to build a big fanbase for several years. The idea was to follow a group of outcast students who find a way to express themselves through music. The story initially centers on Will Schuester (Matthew Morrison), a teacher trying to bring McKinley's glee club back to life, who ends up bringing together students who, for different reasons, don't quite fit into the traditional high school environment. And between romances, musical competitions, and the usual teenage drama, the show also touched on subjects like bullying, sexuality, discrimination, and acceptance.

However, Glee had a pretty contradictory relationship with the very messages it was trying to promote. While it encouraged people to embrace their differences, it also relied on jokes about physical appearance, race, disability, and sexual orientation, often making stereotypes a central part of its humor. Who could forget cheerleading coach Sue Sylvester (Jane Lynch)? As funny as she could be, most of her comedy revolved around insults and offensive remarks, a type of humor that just wouldn't work the same way today. The problem isn't that the series made politically incorrect jokes or featured unlikeable characters, but that it often failed to recognize the difference between making fun of prejudice and actually reproducing it. And now it's set to get a reboot —but some fans are already worried about it.
